*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vitakka Sutta* ("Thoughts", Iti 38; It 2.11, PTS It 31) is a discourse found in the *Itivuttaka* of the Khuddaka Nikāya. The text sets forth two distinct thoughts that habitually arise in the Buddha as he dwells delighting in non-ill will and seclusion.

  The sutta is additionally cited in exegetical canonical texts, including the *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), and *Mogharājamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 19).

DharmaNexus also aligns the text cross-linguistically with the Sanskrit *Mahāvadānasūtra*, the Sanskrit and Tibetan *Udānavarga*, and the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26) [DharmaNexus].
